title: Helly selection: no limiting mass concentration at levels outside a countable set
statement: Let μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) be Borel measures on ℝ, let a, b ∈ ℝ and let Λ ∈ [0, ∞) satisfy μ_j([a, b]) ≤ Λ for every j. Then there exist a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and a countable set N ⊆ ℝ such that for every s ∈ (a, b) with s ∉ N and every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is δ > 0 with μ_{φ(j)}([s − δ, s]) ≤ ε for all sufficiently large j.
lean_statement: ∀ (μ : ℕ → Measure ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (Λ : ℝ≥0∞), Λ ≠ ∞ → (∀ j, μ j (Icc a b) ≤ Λ) → ∃ (φ : ℕ → ℕ) (N : Set ℝ), StrictMono φ ∧ N.Countable ∧ ∀ s ∈ Ioo a b, s ∉ N → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ᶠ j in atTop, μ (φ j) (Icc (s - δ) s) ≤ ε
